=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1747-1761 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: On the final attempt, a `fix` is classified as a merge action and can be held by the security gate before its fix commit is pushed; the hold message also describes the fix as a merge.
  WHY: This can leave the PR on the unchanged head and repeatedly hold the fix; deepseek describes the gate behavior as intentional and flags the misleading operator message, while the other reviewers report the blocked fix as a defect.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2095-2111 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The security extension marker is posted before the fix commit is pushed, so a failed push can leave a marker that grants an audit cycle for a commit that never reached the branch.
  WHY: `single_pass_extensions` counts the marker without verifying that its referenced commit reached the branch (`scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:141–146`); severity assessments range from NIT to MAJOR.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2109-2111 | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: After the extension marker posts but the push fails, the script warns and exits successfully without setting `judge_handled=true`.
  WHY: The workflow wrapper can report `rb_judge_status=ok` although the fix did not land, and the linked issues then go to `ai:review-blocked`.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_security_pass.py:235-237 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The test function name `test_extension_marker_failure_only_warns` contradicts its assertion that the failure is fatal.
  WHY: The contradictory name can mislead maintainers about the fail-closed behavior the test actually verifies.
- scripts/review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh:86-106 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: No defect is reported; the reviewer notes that an empty findings file proceeds into security-exhaustion mode and identifies this as intended behavior.
  WHY: The reviewer says the empty-string branch is informational and that no change is needed.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: A merge the judge decides after autofix exhaustion goes through the security gate; a clean audit allows the merge, otherwise the merge is held while the audit runs and the judge decides again when the review reruns.
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh action-dispatch block and the PR description, README.md, agents.md, and changelog fragment
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1750 classifies `fix` on IS_FINAL as a merge action; the PR description, README.md, agents.md, and changelog fragment describe only the merge case, and tests/test_review_rb_judge_security_pass.py covers the `merge` action without pinning the final-attempt `fix` behavior.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1750-1760 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When IS_FINAL=true and the judge chooses fix, the security gate can hold the action before the fix is pushed, while the operator-facing comment says “merge waits” although the judge chose “fix.”
  WHY: The reviewer says the gate behavior is intentional and correctly prevents unaudited code from reaching the branch, but the fix is silently discarded and the operator message mismatches the judge action.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2095-2111 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The extension marker is posted before the push, so a failed push leaves a marker that raises the cycle budget for a fix that never reached the branch.
  WHY: The gate may spend a cycle auditing an unchanged head.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:2109-2111 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the push fails after the marker posts, the script only warns and does not set judge_handled=true.
  WHY: The script exits 0 and the workflow wrapper can set rb_judge_status=ok despite the fix not landing.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: From the PR description: "A merge the judge decides after autofix runs out used to bypass the security pass. It now goes through the same gate: - A clean audit of the current commit: the PR merges. - Otherwise: the merge is held (judge_action=security_hold) while the audit runs, and the judge decides again when the audit re-runs the review."
  Expected change site: The PR description, README, and changelog fragment name only "merge" going through the gate, not "fix at IS_FINAL." The code at review_rb_judge.sh:1746-1750 additionally classifies fix at IS_FINAL as a merge action for the security gate, which is documented in the code comment but not in the PR description or external docs.
  Evidence of absence: The PR description section "3. Judge merges no longer skip the security pass" and the README documentation describe only merge and merge_with_followup actions passing through the gate. Neither mentions that fix + IS_FINAL = true is also treated as a merge for security-gate purposes. The code comment at line 1746 documents it, but external-facing docs and the changelog fragment omit this case.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: [code reference: case "${RB_ACTION}" in merge|merge_with_followup) RB_MERGE_ACTION="true" ;; fix) [ "${IS_FINAL}" = "true" ] && RB_MERGE_ACTION="true" ;; esac] | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A final-attempt fix action is reclassified as a merge action and held by the security gate instead of allowing the fix to be pushed.
  WHY: If the judge chooses fix on the final attempt, the `rb_security_merge_gate` will hold the action, preventing the fix from being pushed and potentially leaving the PR stuck.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: [code reference: if ! rb_security_post_extension ...; then exit 42; fi; ...; if git push ...; then ...] | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The security extension marker is posted before the commit is pushed.
  WHY: If marker publication succeeds but the subsequent git push fails, the marker persists in the PR history, granting an unnecessary audit cycle for a commit that was never pushed to the PR branch.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: A merge the judge decides after autofix exhaustion also goes through this gate (outside security-exhaustion mode): a clean audit of the head merges, otherwise the judge's merge is held (`judge_action=security_hold`) while the audit runs, and the judge decides again when the audit re-runs the review. Security-mode merges skip the gate, because the pass is already spent.
  Expected change site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh (the action dispatch) plus the PR description / agents.md / changelog fragment
  Evidence of absence: The PR description, README, agents.md, and changelog fragment describe only the merge case; they do not mention that a final-attempt `fix` action is reclassified as a merge-hold.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: lines 1747-1761 (the RB_MERGE_ACTION classification and gate block), in concert with lines 2088-2111 (the fix action dispatch) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When IS_FINAL=true and the judge picks fix, the security gate checks the old head and can prevent the staged fix commit from being pushed.
  WHY: The reviewer says the gate verdict prematurely blocks a fix intended to change the head, and the operator-facing log says "merge held" rather than "fix held."
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh and scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh lines 2095-2111 (extension post then push) and scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh lines 137-150 + 235-239 + 268-291 (the `single_pass_extensions` counter and the exhaustion branch) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The extension marker is posted before the push, and `single_pass_extensions` counts markers without verifying that the referenced head SHA reached the branch.
  WHY: The marker can raise the cycle budget for an unpushed fix, causing an audit or awaiting-followups path to consume the budget without the fix landing.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_security_pass.py: line 235 (the `test_extension_marker_failure_only_warns` test function) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The function name says `_only_warns` while its assertion requires a nonzero result and an error.
  WHY: The reviewer identifies this as a maintainability hazard; the comment says the rename was intentionally skipped.
- scripts/review_rb_judge_security_pass.sh: lines 86-106 (rb_security_findings_render — the new pagination + parse path) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: No defect is reported; the reviewer notes that an empty findings file proceeds with security-exhaustion mode and calls this intended behavior.
  WHY: The reviewer says no change is needed.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "A merge the judge decides after autofix exhaustion also goes through this gate (outside security-exhaustion mode): a clean audit of the head merges, otherwise the judge's merge is held (`judge_action=security_hold`) while the audit runs, and the judge decides again when the audit re-dispatches the review. Security-mode merges skip the gate, because the pass is already spent." (PR Description section 3; mirrored in README.md, agents.md, and changelog.d/autofix-cap-and-security-exhaustion-judge.md.)
  Expected change site: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh — the gate classification must read "a judge merge" as `merge | merge_with_followup` only. Either (a) the line `fix) [ "${IS_FINAL}" = "true" ] && RB_MERGE_ACTION="true" ;;` is removed and the `fix` action at IS_FINAL is allowed to push without going through the security merge gate, or (b) the user-facing contract (PR description, README, agents.md, changelog fragment) is updated to say that a final-attempt `fix` is also reclassified as `judge_action=security_hold` and the fix is *not* pushed.
  Evidence of absence: scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:1750 has the `fix) [ "${IS_FINAL}" = "true" ] && RB_MERGE_ACTION="true" ;;` arm; no other call site, test, or doc explains it. The PR description's section 3, README.md (the new security-exhaustion warning block at lines 519-525), agents.md's `RB_JUDGE_SECURITY_PASS` log-prefix entry at lines 1228-1229 ("a judge merge waited for the single-issue security pass"), and the changelog fragment all describe only the merge path. tests/test_review_rb_judge_security_pass.py covers `test_judge_merge_goes_through_the_security_gate` for the `merge` action, with no test pinning the `fix) [ "${IS_FINAL}" = "true" ] && RB_MERGE_ACTION="true" ;;` arm — leaving the divergent behaviour silently uncontracted.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh: 2095–2110; the extension marker is posted before `git push`, and a failed push only logs a warning. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A concurrent update can reject the push after the durable extension marker has already been posted.
  WHY: `single_pass_extensions` counts trusted markers without checking whether their referenced commit reached the PR branch (`scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:141–146`). The review-blocked judge then holds a merge for the security pass; the deferred push step does not retry this judge commit unless `DID_COMMIT` or `CONFLICT_RESOLVED` is true (`.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:6046`).
=== END FINDINGS FR
